articles.headline: Struggling Man United humbled in Champions League rout at Italian upstarts Como
articles.description: Manchester United's struggling start to the season hit a new low on Wednesday with a 4-1 thrashing at Italian upstarts Como in the Champions League, to pile further pressure on coach Michael Carrick.
articles.headlineJa: 低迷するマンチェスター・ユナイテッド、CLでイタリアの新興勢力コモに完敗
articles.descriptionJa: 低迷しているマンチェスター・ユナイテッドの今シーズンは、水曜日のチャンピオンズリーグでイタリアの新興勢力コモに1-4で大敗し、さらなるどん底に落ちた。これにより、マイケル・キャリック監督への圧力はさらに高まっている。
articles.body:
Manchester United's struggling start to the season hit a new low on Wednesday with a 4-1 thrashing at Italian upstarts Como in the Champions League, to pile further pressure on coach Michael Carrick.

The under-fire United coach had said that Sunday's purposeful point at rivals Leeds marked a "fresh start" after Lisandro Martínez highlighted the club's shortcomings in a set of stunning interviews last week.

But, looking to end a run of six games without a win, Carrick's side got off to the worst possible start in the idyllic surroundings on the shores of Lake Como, when Nico Paz scored inside two minutes. The goal meant that United became the first English club in Champions League history to concede a goal in the first two minutes in back-to-back matches, following last week's loss to Atlético Madrid.

Further goals from Anastasios Douvikas, Paz again and Jacobo Ramón in the second half had the three-time winners set to match their worst ever loss in the history of Europe's premier competition before Joshua Zirkzee grabbed a consolation goal in stoppage time.

It is still just the sixth ever loss by three-plus goals in Manchester United's Champions League history and the first since April 2019 against Barcelona in the quarterfinals.

In contrast to Man United's rich pedigree in the competition, Como, coached by former Arsenal and Barcelona great Cesc Fabregas, are taking part in a European competition for the first time in their 119-year history.

Wednesday's victory meant Como become the first Italian club to win their first two home games in the Champions League since Lazio in 1999-2000.

Paz has been auditioning to take over Lionel Messi's playmaker spot with Argentina and his performance against United was a case in point.

At the tiny 10,000-seat Giuseppe Sinigaglia stadium, Paz put Como ahead with a curling shot from the edge of the area when Harry Maguire allowed him some space.

Douvikas then took a pass from Paz before lobbing in over goalkeeper Senne Lammens for his third goal in three Champions League matches.

For Como's third, Paz went in virtually uncontested before shooting around Lammens. Center back Jacobo Ramón scored Como's fourth.

Despite Zirkzee's late goal off the bench, United have won only one of their last 11 Champions League away matches.

Como moved up to sixth in the standings, while United dropped to 20th.

Information from ESPN Research, The Associated Press and PA contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Raheem Morris is back in Atlanta -- and he's bringing his surging 49ers defense
articles.description: Raheem Morris is returning to Atlanta for the first time since being fired as head coach. And his tenure as the 49ers' defensive coordinator is off to an amazing start.
articles.headlineJa: ラヒーム・モリスがアトランタに帰還 —— 絶好調の49ersディフェンスと共に
articles.descriptionJa: ラヒーム・モリスが、ヘッドコーチを解任されて以来、初めてアトランタに戻ってくる。49ersのディフェンシブコーディネーターとしての任期は、素晴らしいスタートを切っている。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Upon his return to Mercedes-Benz Stadium on Sunday, Raheem Morris won't head toward the home locker room as the coach of the Atlanta Falcons. Instead, he will veer in the opposite direction as the San Francisco 49ers' defensive coordinator.

Six games into his tenure with the 49ers, Morris -- who spent the past two years as Atlanta's head coach -- isn't worried about how to get back into the top chair. His top priority is leading a surging defense that has already surpassed expectations. It's why, when asked last week whether he hoped to get a third crack at becoming a head coach, Morris quickly brushed the idea aside.

"We have somewhere in society been screwed up," Morris said. "We have got this illusion in our head that everybody's a head coach. There are 32 head coaches in the National Football League. There are 32 defensive coordinators, and there are 32 offensive coordinators, and there's 32 everything we do. ... We are blessed and you couldn't have a better job than all of us."

Morris' return to Atlanta provides an ideal backdrop to examine the effect he has had on a San Francisco defense that is on its fifth coordinator in as many years. With some minor but notable schematic changes to unlock a more aggressive secondary and productive front, his group provided game-winning sequences the past two weeks against Seattle and Washington. And the numbers through six undefeated weeks speak for themselves.

This season, the 49ers have allowed the fewest explosive plays (rushes of 10-plus yards and passes of 20-plus yards) in the NFL. They rank fourth in points allowed per game (18.3) and yards allowed per play (4.7). They're also fifth in total yards allowed per game (300) and defensive expected points added (21.59), as well as seventh in ESPN's defensive efficiency metric (64.95).

Most of that production has come without star DE Nick Bosa (calf), as well as DT Alfred Collins (patellar tendon), DT C.J. West (knee) and DE Sam Okuayinonu (foot). Which is why safety Ji'Ayir Brown said that with a little injury luck and more time on task with Morris, San Francisco's defense can be even better the rest of the way.

"Honestly, I think we can be No. 1 in all categories, but it is a new defense," Brown said. "It is a lot of figuring things out."

Brown's belief is rooted largely in the improvement of his position group. Despite the occasional hiccup, the Niners have continuity from last season at safety (Malik Mustapha and Marques Sigle) and cornerback (Renardo Green, Deommodore Lenoir and Upton Stout). During training camp, all players in the secondary pointed to Morris' schematic tweaks as allowing them to play more freely in coverage.

articles.headline: Who could replace Carrick after Man United's worst start since 1986?
articles.description: Manchester United have struggled this season, but which managers could step in to replace Michael Carrick if the club sacks him?
articles.headlineJa: 1986年以来の最悪のスタートを切ったマン・ユナイテッド、キャリックの後任は誰に？
articles.descriptionJa: 今シーズン苦戦しているマンチェスター・ユナイテッドだが、もしクラブがマイケル・キャリックを解任した場合、どの監督が後任として就任する可能性があるか。
articles.body:
Manchester United have made their worst start to a league season since 1986. They exited the Carabao Cup at the first hurdle last month and are closer to the Premier League relegation zone than the top four following Sunday's 1-1 draw at Leeds United, so the pressure is mounting on manager Michael Carrick.

That trip to Elland Road extended United's winless run in all competitions to six games, though Carrick said that the result against Daniel Farke's side marked a "fresh start" for his team. But Wednesday's UEFA Champions League trip to Serie A's Como provided no respite, as United hit a new low with the 4-1 loss.

United have dismissed a manager in each of the past two seasons -- Erik ten Hag was fired in October 2024, followed by Ruben Amorim in January 2026.

So with results continuing to disappoint and Carrick, who guided United to Champions League qualification as interim manager last season, struggling to prove he is the man for the job in the long term, who are the most likely candidates to replace the 45-year-old at Old Trafford if he fails to inspire a change of fortune?

Here are the managers who could be on United's radar -- and the prospects of them being the next one to take on one of the sport's biggest, and toughest, jobs.

Eddie Howe (unattached)

Positives

The 48-year-old is taking a break from the game after stepping down as Newcastle United manager in August following almost five years in charge. During his time at St James' Park, Howe saved the club from relegation before guiding the team to Champions League qualification on two occasions and ending a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy by winning the Carabao Cup in 2025.

Howe is a proven Premier League manager with a track record at Newcastle and Bournemouth. He is a team builder, tactically astute and his ability to transform the fortunes of players like Joelinton and Dan Burn at Newcastle would appeal to United, whose squad is stacked with players who are failing to live up to their potential. Another key element with Howe is his immediate availability.

Negatives

Howe will deliver stability and consistency wherever he manages, but does he possess the X factor for a club of United's magnitude? That is perhaps a harsh question to ask of a coach whose credentials are without question, but United need a coach to lift the whole club and its fan base. Howe's "Steady Eddie" persona might be exactly what they need, but also what they really don't need right now.

That strange dilemma is probably why United are in the mess they are in. They need the stability and calmness -- and direction -- that Howe would bring, but they also need a personality to become the focal point and leader of a club that has lost direction. Howe wins on the basics, but United need more than that.

Suitability rating

3/5: Howe would be a sensible appointment, but that isn't enough for Manchester United.

articles.headline: Como embarrass Man United as rout adds to Carrick pressure
articles.description: Manchester United fell to one of the most embarrassing European defeats in their history as Champions League upstarts Como ran out 4-1 victors on Wednesday.
articles.headlineJa: コモがマン・ユナイテッドに屈辱的な敗戦を突きつけ、キャリックへの圧力増大
articles.descriptionJa: 水曜日のチャンピオンズリーグで、新興勢力のコモが4-1で勝利したことで、マンチェスター・ユナイテッドは欧州舞台における歴史上最も屈辱的な敗戦の一つを喫した。
articles.body:
Manchester United fell to one of the most embarrassing European defeats in their history as Champions League upstarts Como ran out 4-1 victors on Wednesday to heap pressure on head coach Michael Carrick.

The under-fire Red Devils boss had felt Sunday's purposeful point at rivals Leeds marked a "fresh start" after Lisandro Martínez highlighted the club's shortcomings in a set of stunning interviews last week.

But United instead saw their wretched start to the season hit a new low on Wednesday as Cesc Fabregas' Como punished a display devoid of shape, grit and skill to extend their winless run to a seventh match.

This humbling loss puts Carrick's future under intense scrutiny, with the storm that battered the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia nothing compared to the one brewing at Old Trafford.

United made a nightmare start, just as they did at Atletico Madrid last week, as burgeoning star Nico Paz struck against a side that were shaky out of possession and shapeless with it.

Carrick's side were fortunate to only be a goal behind at the break and their luck soon ran out, with Tasos Douvikas' strike followed by Paz scoring his second and Jacobo Ramón heading home.

Substitute Joshua Zirkzee added a consolation goal on a night that ended with Carrick holding his hands up apologetically in front of those United fans that stayed until the end.

articles.headline: Patriots' Alijah Vera-Tucker, Ben Brown ruled out vs. Bears
articles.description: The Patriots will be without starting guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown for Thursday's game against the Bears due to injuries, coach Mike Vrabel said.
articles.headlineJa: パトリオッツのアリジャ・ヴェラ＝タッカーとベン・ブラウン、ベアーズ戦を欠場
articles.descriptionJa: マイク・ヴラベル監督は、怪我のため、木曜日のベアーズ戦に先発ガードのアリジャ・ヴェラ＝タッカーとベン・ブラウンが出場しないことを明らかにした。
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- The New England Patriots will be without starting guards Alijah Vera-Tucker and Ben Brown for Thursday's road game against the Chicago Bears due to injuries, coach Mike Vrabel said.

Vera-Tucker played every snap this season at left guard before injuring his hamstring in the second quarter of Sunday's win over the New York Jets, his former team. Brown, meanwhile, was the third right guard to start -- after Mike Onwenu and Greg Van Roten both landed on injured reserve -- and he hobbled off in the second half of Sunday's game with a knee injury.

Vrabel said Walter Rouse, a three-year veteran acquired in a trade from the Minnesota Vikings on Aug. 30, will start at left guard. It will be his first career NFL start.

Vrabel said nine-year veteran Matt Pryor, whom the Patriots signed off the Arizona Cardinals' practice squad on Oct. 1, will start at right guard. He has started 40 career games, with 15 of them coming in the 2024 season with the Chicago Bears.

Quarterback Drake Maye wasn't sacked in Sunday's win, and he credited the offensive line -- which also played without veteran right tackle Morgan Moses (foot) for two-plus quarters - for exemplary work.

"I feel like it's been every week somebody stepping up," Maye said. "On the flip side of it, it's unfortunate seeing so many of our guys go down. I'm impressed with how the coaches have been handling it, of kind of moving personnel around and fixing things on the sideline and adjusting."

Moses was limited in practice in recent days, but Vrabel said he has a chance to play against the Bears.

The Patriots (4-2), who also placed starting receiver Romeo Doubs (shoulder) on injured reserve Monday and will be without starting cornerback Carlton Davis III (neck) for the third game in a row, have won three straight games.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 21: J.J. McCarthy named Giants' starting QB for Week 7

By Tristan H. Cockcroft

The inevitable has finally arrived in New York: McCarthy is reportedly going to start at quarterback for the Giants in Week 7.

It was a decision destined to happen at some point following McCarthy's Sept. 28 acquisition from the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a 2027 fifth-round pick. And it was a decision almost assuredly destined to happen this week after the Michigan product delivered 16.52 fantasy points in the fourth quarter alone, nearly leading his Giants to a comeback from down 34-10 to the Saints.

McCarthy's installation doesn't promise any miracles, not for the Giants nor for fantasy, but it's an understandable, aggressive move that could positively shift the team's offensive dynamic.

First off, don't take McCarthy's Week 6 performance remotely to heart, as it's almost entirely meaningless for evaluative purposes. High-scoring relief efforts by quarterbacks aren't uncommon. Since 2021, there have been 13 relief performances of 15 or more fantasy points by quarterbacks who made a start later in that season; that group averaged 5.2 fewer fantasy points as starters than in that relief appearance.

More relevant to McCarthy's cause is his extensive tape from his 10 mediocre (to say it gently) starts in Minnesota last season. In those starts, he was 28th in Total QBR (36.1), 30th in completion rate (57.6%), 28th in off-target rate (19.3%) and 30th in touchdown-to-interception ratio (0.9). He struggled mightily when throwing into crowded spaces, with the fourth-worst passer rating when targeting a receiver with three or fewer yards of separation, per Next Gen Stats.

What McCarthy did do that could have fantasy-relevance, however, was aim deep about as often as any quarterback in the league. His average depth of target of 8.8 yards led all quarterbacks who started at least half of their teams' games, though he did have seven interceptions on throws of at least 15 yards, putting his skill set into the extreme risk/reward category. Anyone who watched Sunday's game can attest to that, as McCarthy was chucking the ball in a desperate attempt to breathe some life into a Giants offense that, to that point, had shown barely any.

Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely each scored more than half of their Week 6 fantasy points after McCarthy entered the game, and the two combined for five catches on six targets for 130 yards and a touchdown on throws of at least 10 yards from McCarthy. articles.body:
THE CHAMPIONS!

Another day, another round of European heavyweights ready to battle it out on the biggest stage.

Matchday 3 of the 2026-27 UEFA Champions League continues Wednesday, with nine more matches across the continent and plenty of blockbuster clashes to look forward to.

Among the standout fixtures, Arsenal travel to Germany for a heavyweight showdown with Bayern Munich, Real Madrid welcome RB Leipzig to the Bernabéu, and Manchester United went to Italy to face Como in one of our two early matches, only for Michael Carrick's team to lose 4-1 in one of the worst losses in the club's history in the competition.

Also on the schedule, we had Lille vs. Galatasaray in the other early match which saw the Turkish club win 4-2, Club Brugge vs. Lens, Real Betis vs. Feyenoord and Sporting CP vs. LASK.

articles.headline: Sam LaPorta not feeling contract 'love' from Lions ahead of 2027 free agency
articles.description: Tight end Sam LaPorta, who will be a free agent after the season, expressed some frustration that the Lions are "not showing the love" and indicated he would be OK with playing elsewhere in 2027.
articles.headlineJa: サム・ラポータ、2027年のフリーエージェントを前にライオンズからの契約への「愛」を感じず
articles.descriptionJa: 今シーズン後にフリーエージェントとなるタイトエンドのサム・ラポータは、ライオンズが「愛を示していない」ことに不満を表明し、2027年には他チームでプレーしても構わないとの考えを示しました。
articles.body:
Tight end Sam LaPorta let some frustration show over his lack of a contract extension with the Detroit Lions, telling Barstool's "Pardon My Take" podcast that the team is "not showing the love" and indicating he would be OK with playing elsewhere in 2027.

"I'm going to continue to do my thing and ball out, and in three months, if I don't get to wear the Honolulu blue and play for the Lions anymore, it's going to be all good," LaPorta told the podcast. "I'll go get paid somewhere else. So whatever."

LaPorta is playing on the final season of his rookie contract and is set to become a free agent in 2027.

He struck a less diplomatic tone than he did earlier this month, when he described the extension talks as at a stalemate and said he wasn't focused on being the NFL's highest-paid tight end. Those remarks came days after NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Oct. 4 that the side had broken off talks.

In the podcast interview, LaPorta compared his annoyance of playing hard for the Lions, as well as suffering a season-ending back injury in 2025, and not getting rewarded for his performance.

"I think the combination of getting your heartstrings twisted as well as the violent sport that we play, it sucks," LaPorta said. "It's disappointing that you go out there every week and you bear the risk of getting hurt.

"Like last year, whatever it was, Week 9, Week 10, I break my f---ing back for the team. And then I'm going out there this year and I'm balling, and maybe they're just not showing the love."

LaPorta, who was a Pro Bowler and second-time All-Pro as a rookie in 2023, has 27 receptions for 316 yards and three touchdowns this season.

articles.headline: Sources: Warriors exploring options to trade center Kristaps Porzingis
articles.description: The Warriors have begun exploring trade routes for veteran center Kristaps Porzingis, who remains out indefinitely as he deals with a private health issue, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.headlineJa: 関係者：ウォリアーズがセンターのクリスタプス・ポルジンギスのトレード案を検討中
articles.descriptionJa: ウォリアーズは、プライベートな健康問題で無期限欠場となっているベテランセンターのクリスタプス・ポルジンギスのトレードルートを模索し始めたと、リーグ関係者がESPNのシャムス・チャラニアに語りました。
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors have begun exploring trade routes for veteran center Kristaps Porzingis, who remains out indefinitely as he deals with a private health issue that has him seriously contemplating his future in basketball, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Porzingis signed a two-year, $40 million extension with the team in June, but only $3 million of the $20 million in the second season is guaranteed, essentially making it an expiring contract. The front office strategically designed the extension without a raise between the two seasons, keeping him immediately trade-eligible instead of needing to wait until mid-December.

Despite the built-in flexibility, that wasn't the idealized intent of the contract. Porzingis played in 15 of the team's final 20 games last season and Warriors' management believed he had an encouraging enough summer to pencil Porzingis in as the projected starting center next to Draymond Green and rookie Yaxel Lendeborg in the frontcourt.

Porzingis was in the team's San Francisco facility and on the court in the week leading up to training camp and attended Jimmy Butler's player-led event in San Diego in late September, though team sources described a detached Porzingis as indifferent and uninterested in participating in scrimmages and strenuous on-court prep work at the event.

On the Sunday before training camp, Porzingis called the Warriors and alerted general manager Mike Dunleavy that he was still dealing with the lingering impact of a health issue that has bothered him for nearly two years and told them he would be taking an indefinite leave of absence.

Two seasons ago, Porzingis contracted an upper respiratory virus while playing for the Boston Celtics, and he has since vaguely revealed the lingering impact it has had on his energy level and ability to consistently play NBA basketball. Porzingis has termed it a POTS (postural orthostatic tachycardia syndrome) diagnosis, which can lead to bouts of dizziness, fatigue and brain fog.

After missing the first two weeks of training camp and the entire preseason, Porzingis drove up from Los Angeles to San Francisco last Tuesday, league sources said, to meet with Dunleavy and Rick Celebrini, the franchise's lead medical decision-maker.

In the aftermath, the team announced that they would keep the details of the meeting private, but expressed an expectation that Porzingis would remain around the team as he tried to improve his health and eventually resume his career.

But that hasn't been the case. Porzingis hasn't returned to the facility, league sources said, beginning another indefinite leave of absence where he is mostly maintaining contact with only Dunleavy and Celebrini. The Warriors listed him as out for the season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers on Wednesday night and the reasoning as "not with team" instead of an illness.
